bio:
Elise is one of the highest-ranked arms in the class of 2029. She owns the No. 1 ERA in Virginia for her class at 1.30, ranks No. 55 nationally and No. 4 in the Northeast Region in Extra Inning Softball's 2029 pitching rankings, and sits No. 21 nationally on Line Drive Media's Class of 2029 Hot 100.

The numbers hold up across a full year of national competition. In fall 2025 she threw 66.0 innings with 109 strikeouts — 1.65 per inning — against a 1.167 ERA, a .818 WHIP and a .132 opponent average. Over summer 2026 she logged 89.0 innings with 111 strikeouts, a 1.65 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and .186 BAA. She finished tied for 4th on the fall 2025 16U Super Division leaderboard for strikeouts per inning and 4th among Tier 1 pitchers at AFCS Nationals. She works fast, fills the zone, and misses bats without giving away free bases.

At Nansemond-Suffolk Academy she is a two-time VISAA Division II state champion — and as a freshman she was the one who got the ball in the title game. Elise started the 2026 state championship against Christchurch School and went six innings, allowing five hits and three runs, none of them earned, striking out six and walking one in a 7-3 win that gave the Saints their seventh consecutive state title. She had already started the TCIS championship earlier that spring and thrown two no-hit innings with five strikeouts and no walks, then gone 3 2/3 scoreless with five more strikeouts in the VISAA semifinal. A first-team All-State, All-Conference and All-Tidewater selection, she carries a 4.06 GPA with Academic Distinction both semesters and is an Extra Elite Scholar.

bio:
A 2026 NCHSAA 5A state champion as a freshman, Baylee started varsity for Enka High School and led the Sugar Jets in home runs and RBI on their way to the program's fourth state title. Her signature game came in the 5A West Regional Finals, where she hit three home runs — two of them grand slams — in a 12-1 win over North Davidson. In the deciding game of the championship series against West Carteret, her fifth-inning RBI double broke a scoreless tie and sent Enka to a 4-0 win and a 12-game closing streak. She was named to the North Carolina Softball Coaches all-state team as a freshman.

A true utility bat who has played first, third, and the outfield, Baylee carries a 4.3 GPA on an all-honors course load with A honor roll every year since third grade. She plans to study business as a pre-law track toward becoming a family law attorney, and volunteers through Key Club, Special Olympics, and her school's Student Leadership Program.

bio:

Her speed out of the left side puts constant pressure on infield defenses, and her range in the outfield lets her track down balls in the gaps. She has competed in the power and premier pools of top tournaments across the country through the summer circuit.

bio: Keira is a dynamic two-way player who excels at shortstop and on the mound. A switch hitter with excellent bat control, she brings game-changing speed and athleticism to every game. A 2026 VISAA Indoor Track State Champion, she anchored the 4x200 relay to a 1st place finish in 1:43 — breaking both the school record and the state meet record. She also placed 3rd in long jump (16'10.5" PR) and 4th in triple jump (31'9.5"). That elite speed and explosiveness translates directly to the diamond. She represented the US Virgin Islands on the 18U national team.

bio:
A catcher and third baseman for Covenant Day School, Charlotte is a versatile defender whose strong arm and quick release out of the crouch make her a threat to opposing base runners, while her bat provides consistent production in the order. She has been part of a Covenant Day program that put together a five-game win streak including a victory over Charlotte Country Day.

Her ability to handle both premium defensive spots — behind the plate and at the hot corner — gives a coaching staff real lineup flexibility.
achievements: 2026 Alliance Fastpitch 16U Tier III National Runner-Up

bio:
Cara delivered the biggest swing of Pittsford Sutherland's 2026 postseason: a two-out, three-run home run that broke a scoreless tie and lifted the Knights past Eastridge 5-2 for the Section V Class AA2 championship. She also homered in the 13-1 semifinal rout of Pittsford Mendon, and earlier in the season hit two home runs in a single game. She has led Sutherland in home runs two straight years and finished second in the region last year, and was voted a News 8 WROC athlete of the week by area readers.

A multi-sport athlete with elite speed and competitive fire, Cara is also a varsity ski racer — a 4x sectional champion who placed 5th overall at the 2026 Section V Championships. She brings that same explosiveness to the outfield, with exceptional range and the versatility to contribute in the infield.
achievements: 2026 Alliance Fastpitch 16U Tier III National Runner-Up

bio:
The 2026 Tony Bobian Memorial Most Valuable High School Player in Pueblo, Sophia hit .560 as a sophomore shortstop at Pueblo Central with six doubles, six triples, a home run, 13 RBI and 17 stolen bases — striking out just three times in 115 plate appearances. She led Colorado in runs scored with 56.

At shortstop she turned six double plays with 45 putouts and 47 assists, anchoring a Wildcats team that went 22-6, finished 8-0 in the South-Central League for its second straight league title, and reached the state tournament. She was named to the 2025 Colorado all-state team. Softball runs in the family — her father, Jeremiah Perez, is a 2026 Pueblo Softball Hall of Fame inductee and an assistant coach with Stars National Walker.
achievements: 2026 Alliance Fastpitch 16U Tier III National Runner-Up
recruitingNotes: Creighton is #1 school. Loved Purdue coaching staff. USF came to game. Penn State and Penn watched her play.

bio:
A 6'1" freshman catcher at Marvin Ridge, Riley hit .434 with 24 RBI and was named First Team All-Conference in the Southern Carolina 6A/7A, NCSCA Region 6 7A All-District, and NCSCA 7A All-State. Extra Inning Softball ranks her No. 14 in the Southeast and No. 38 among catchers nationally in the Class of 2029. She was also named to the 2025 PGF Premier Nationals All-Tournament Team.

Behind the plate she brings soft hands, quiet receiving, and the arm to control the running game — plus the presence to run a pitching staff. She was Marvin Ridge's 2026 Team Rookie of the Year.

bio:
Contact-first outfielder with plus speed and a plus arm. A multi-sport athlete who competes in outdoor track — triple jump, sprints, and relays — the same explosiveness and top-end speed that make her dangerous on the bases and in the gaps. At the 5A Georgia Meet on Feb. 11, she ran an 8.86 laser-timed 60m, finishing 18th out of 71 competitors. She's also a key leg on her school's 4x100m relay, typically closing the gap as a strong curve runner.

Played the full 2025 summer on an 18U team, traveling the Northeast for major tournaments including TNT and New England's Finest, where she started in center field and hit leadoff all summer. She joined Stars National Walker at PGF Nationals, starting in the outfield and batting .400 for the tournament with multiple stolen bases.

Athletic family: Both parents were student-athletes at the University of Georgia. Dad (Mike) played football; Mom (Karin) was an All-American gymnast.

Natalie announced herself with a perfect game in her very first varsity start — striking out 14 of the 15 batters she faced in Huntingtown's 20-0 win over Westlake as a freshman. Across her 2026 high school season she threw 16 innings with 35 strikeouts, zero walks, and a 0.00 ERA, allowing just two hits.

A left-handed pitcher and first baseman with elite command, she is a 2026 USA Softball All-American and a Line Drive Media Top 100 player in the Class of 2029, and helped drive Huntingtown's run back to the Maryland state finals. Off the field she carries a 4.1 GPA on the Honor Roll and captains her high school volleyball team.

bio:
A sophomore catcher and utility player at Mineral Point, Austyn hit .563 across 31 games in 2026 with a .605 on-base percentage. She finished with 58 hits — 15 doubles and eight home runs — drove in 40 runs, and was a perfect 21-for-21 on stolen bases.

Line Drive Media named her a [2026 1st Team High School All-American catcher](https://linedrivemedia.com/news/high-school-honors-the-2026-live-drive-softball-1st-team-high-school-all-americans-catchers-july-7-2026/). She was also a Line Drive National High School Player of the Week runner-up, plus 1st Team All-District and 1st Team All-State. As a freshman she was 1st Team All-State, All-District, and All-Conference, helping Mineral Point reach the WIAA Division 4 state tournament for the second time in program history — she homered in the sectional final shutout of Waterloo that punched their ticket. Extra Inning Softball rates her a Top 25 Slugger and the No. 100 catcher nationally. She wears #44 for Stars National Walker.
